question.text: Under the earlier transaction charge framework (before its withdrawal in August 2025), what happened when an investor invested less than Rs. 10,000 through a distributor?

answer.text: A reduced transaction charge of Rs. 50 was applicable
The transaction charge was proportionately reduced based on the investment amount
The distributor had to absorb the transaction charge from their commission
No transaction charge was applicable for investments below Rs. 10,000

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the earlier framework, AMCs were allowed to pay transaction charges only for subscriptions worth more than Rs. 10,000 (workbook p. 127). For investments below Rs. 10,000, no transaction charge applied. The framework itself was withdrawn by the August 2025 SEBI circular, so no investor-borne transaction charges are deducted under the current regime (workbook pp. 123 and 127). The Trap: Option A invents a Rs. 50 charge tier that is not in the workbook. Option B assumes a sliding scale, when the rule was a single threshold. Option C wrongly puts the cost on the distributor. Note: Use the workbook's exact wording — the prior rule applied to subscriptions "more than Rs. 10,000", not "Rs. 10,000 or more"; and remember the framework has since been withdrawn.
